## Japan — Press and Publications: Leading Newspapers

### Leading Newspapers

**Chugai Shogyo Shimpo** (started in 1876). Economic and Commercial paper, issues both morning and evening editions, Pres., T. Tanaka; Ed., T. Obama. Office—Kayaba-cho, Nihombashi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 174 ([scan part 1, leaf 231](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n231/mode/1up))

**Hochi Shimbun** (started in 1872). Issues both morning and evening editions. Pres., S. Noma; Ed., S. Okano. Office—Yurakucho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 174 ([scan part 1, leaf 231](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n231/mode/1up))

**Jiji Shimpo** (started in 1882). Amalgamated into Tokyo Nichi Nichi in December, 1936. — p. 174 ([scan part 1, leaf 231](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n231/mode/1up))

**Kokumin Shimbun** (started in 1892). Founded by Iichiro Tokutomi who retired in 1928; issues both morning and evening editions. Pres., M. Shiki; Ed., I. Yamanouchi. Office—Ginza-Nishi 7-chome, Kyobashi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 174 ([scan part 1, leaf 231](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n231/mode/1up))

**Miyako Shimbun** (started in 1885). Social paper, Pres., E. Fukuda, Ed., H. Watanabe. Office—Uchisaiwaicho 1-chome, Kojimachi-ku Tokyo. — p. 174 ([scan part 1, leaf 231](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n231/mode/1up))

**Tokyo Asahi Shimbun** (started in 1888). Sister paper to the Osaka Asahi Shimbun; issues boht morning and evening editions. Pres., S. Uyeno; Ed., T. Ogata. Office—Yurakucho 2-chome Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 174 ([scan part 1, leaf 231](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n231/mode/1up))

## Japan — Social Problems: Organs for Control, Deliberation and Arbitration (private institutes)

### Organs for Control, Deliberation and Arbitration

**The Kyocho-kai (Tokyo)** Organized in 1919 by the Government authorities, university professors, business men, social workers, etc., to effect the “harmonization of capital and labour.” — p. 221 ([scan part 1, leaf 280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n280/mode/1up))

**Ohara Social Problems Research Institute (Osaka)** Established in 1919 by Mr. Ohara, a millionaire in Okayama, it conducts all important researches on social problems in the country, the staff including Dr. Iwasaburo Takano (Chief) and a number of able experts. — p. 221 ([scan part 1, leaf 280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n280/mode/1up))

**Kurashiki Institute for the Research of the Science of Labour (Kurashiki, Okayama prefecture)** Also founded by Mr. Ohara. Investigates the scientific aspects of the labour problem. — p. 221 ([scan part 1, leaf 280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n280/mode/1up))

**Industrial Labour Investigation Office (Tokyo)** Established in 1924, chiefly by representatives of labour organizations and scholars, to investigate political, economic and social affairs of the country. — p. 221 ([scan part 1, leaf 280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n280/mode/1up))

**Arima's Agrarian Research Institute (Tokyo)** Established by Count R. Arima to devote itself to the study of agrarian problems, which are now growing in importance and attracting the serious attention of the public, in consequence of the wide awakening of the peasant class. — p. 221 ([scan part 1, leaf 280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n280/mode/1up))


## Japan — Shipping and Shipbuilding: Leading Shipowners (company notes)

### Leading Shipowners

**Nippon Yusen Kaisha (Japan Mail S.S. Co.)** Founded in October, 1885, the Nippon Yusen Kaisha, which is the premier maritime company of Japan, celebrated the jubilee in October, 1935. The company was established by the amalgamation of two rival concerns, the Mitsubishi and the Kyodo Un-yu Kaisha, which were in cut-throat competition with each other. By the amalgamation of the two companies the N. Y. K. inherited 29 steamers and 1 sailing vessels from the Mitsubishi Company and 29 steamers and 10 sailing craft from the Kyodo Un-yu Kaisha, making a total of 69 vessels. Of these the 58 steamers totalled 64,610 tons gross and the 11 sailing vessels 4,725 tons gross. Between Japan and New York the Company maintains what is one of the most up-to-date freight services on the oceans to-day. The company put into commission in the Jubilee Year six new motor vessels on its Orient-New York Express Service. These six sister ships are all of 9,000 tons and their speed 18½ knots. Three of them were built in Nagasaki and three in Yokohama. The company owns several motorships on its Pacific run. These are the Chichibu maru (17,500 tons), the Asama Maru (17,000 tons) and the Tatsuta Maru (17,000 tons). These, along with the Taiyo Maru, run a fast fortnightly service from Hong-Kong to Los Angeles and San Francisco, via Honolulu. On the European run the company has also excellent boats, the Terukuni Maru and the Yasukuni Maru being the finest ships on the service. They are both of 11,900 tons gross. As on March 31, 1937 the company owned 87 steamers, totalling 635,280 tons gross . The following is a list of the important N.Y.K. passenger and freight services:— Japan-European Fortnightly Service; Orient-California Fortnightly Service; Japan-Australia Monthly Service; South American West Coast Monthly Service; Japan-Bombay Monthly Service; Japan-China Rapid Express Service. Besides the above the company maintains regular passenger services from Japan to Tsingtao, the South Sea Islands, Tientsin, Formosa, etc., the last two being operated by the N. Y. K. Line. The authorized capital of the company is ¥106,250,000, ¥78,250,000 paid up. — p. 261 ([scan part 1, leaf 320](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n320/mode/1up))

**Osaka Shosen Kaisha (Osaka Mercantile S.S. Co.)** The Company was established in 1884 by the amalgamation of small shipping companies which had steamers plying between ports in the inland sea. The field of operation has subsequently been enlarged. The following is a list of the important O. S. K. passenger and freight services in operation in the first half of 1937:— South American Monthly Service; New York Rapid Express Monthly Service; East Coast African Monthly Service; Bombay Twice Monthly Service; Calcutta Twice Monthly Service; Australia Monthly Service; South Seas Service (South Seas Subsidized Service, South Seas Voluntary Service, Philippine Service, Saigon-Bangkok Service). The Company also maintains a regular passenger service from Japan to important places in Formosa, China, Korea, Dairen, etc. As on March 31, 1937 the Company owned 107 steamers aggregating 502,992 tons gross. The authorized capital of the Company is ¥100,000,000, of which ¥62,500,000 is paid up. — p. 261 ([scan part 1, leaf 320](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n320/mode/1up))


## Japan — Shipping and Shipbuilding: Principal Tramp-Owners

### Principal Tramp-Owners

**Kokusai Line (International S.S. Co.)** In order to meet an astounding increase in the demand for bottoms during the World War both shipowners and shipyards built one ship after another. Shipyards even went the length of building ships without any order. As the activity of the freight market during the war was spectacular, so the reaction that followed the Armistice was serious. It was for the purpose of relieving the shipowners and shipbuilders of the acute pain caused by a serious break of the price of ships that the Kokusai Kisen Kaisha was organized in 1919 with the surplus of the vessels thus built during the war, through the good offices of the Government. As in July, 1937 the Company operated regular freight services between the Far East and North Europe, New York and Hamburg, Japan and Australia, Japan and East and South Africa, Japan and Bombay, Japan and Formosa. Three 19-knotters which were completed in 1936 have been allocated to the newly inaugurated Far East-North Europe fast service, which maintains four-weekly sailing in conjunction with two new freighters of the N. Y. K. Furthermore, five motor and turbine super-freighters of about 9,200 tons deadweight each are now on order with the shipbuilders in Japan and will all be completed before the end of 1938. The Company owns motor and steam vessels amounting to 300,000 tons gross. Mr. Shinjiro Kurokawa, formerly vice-President of the N. Y. K. is President. The Company is capitalized at ¥80,000,000 and under its able president cleared net profits of over ¥4,160,000 for the year ending December 31, 1936. — p. 265 ([scan part 1, leaf 324](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n324/mode/1up))

**Yamashita Kisen Kaisha (Yamashita S.S. Co.)** The Company was founded in 1902 by Mr. Kamesaburo Yamashita. The activity of the Company during the World War was worldwide. As on March 31, 1937 the Company owned 14 ships amounting to 82,400 tons gross. The Yamashita Kisen is the largest of the five major companies operating trampers, the other four being Daido, Mitsui, Kawasaki, Kokusai. In May, 1937 the Company increased its capital from ¥20,320,500 to ¥35,000,000. The Company's shipping operation extends to South Seas, Australia, Europe, North America and Africa. One of its noteworthy service is the transportation of Saghalien timber to Japan and Manchuria beans to Europe. — p. 265 ([scan part 1, leaf 324](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n324/mode/1up))

**Mitsui Line** The Mitsui Line operates regular and irregular services. The former consists of the direct New York service, the Bangkok service, the Indian service (Bombay and Madras), the Philippine service, Dairen service, the Iran Bay service and the Moji-Yokohama service. The latter represents many ports in Europe, North America, South America, Australia, Africa, British India, the South Seas and Japan. As on March 31, 1937 the Mitsui Line owned 35 steamers amounting to 149,690 tons gross. — p. 265 ([scan part 1, leaf 324](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n324/mode/1up))

**Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha** The Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha is one of the seven largest shipping companies of Japan. It was founded in April, 1919 with a capital of ¥20,000,000, which is paid up. Principal regular services operated by the Company are the New York Line, San Francisco-Los Angeles Line, Seatle-Vancouver Line, Japan-Australia Line, Europe-Far East Line, Tokyo-Yokohama-Dairen Line, North Korea Line, South America (West Coast) Line, East and South Africa Line, Bombay Line, Asia-Europe-North and South America Line. As on March 31, 1937 the Company owned 15 ships aggregating 63,351 tons gross. — p. 265 ([scan part 1, leaf 324](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n324/mode/1up))


## Japan — Banking: Special banks

### Special Banks

**The Bank of Japan** (Head Office—Hongoku-cho, Nihonbashi, Tokyo). Established 1882. Authorized capital is ¥60,000,000, of which ¥45,000,000 is paid up. Deposits ¥386,748,119.040, of which the Government's are ¥293,178,726.229 including Current Account for ¥162,421,679.281. Advances ¥791,014,808.010 (inclusive of bills discounted), of which ¥232,600,434.380 is to the Government, Reserve fund ¥115,690,000.000, Divid., 10% p.a., Note issue ¥1,640,832,571.500. The Bank of Japan may issue bank notes to any extent against specie reserve of gold and silver; provided that the value of silver shall not exceed one-fourth of the total. The Bank is also authorise dto make fiduciary issue against Government bonds or other specified securities up to ¥1,000,000,000. An additional fiduciary issue over and above this limit may be made; provided, however, that in case such an excess issue is to continue beyond 15 days the Bank shall obtain the approval of the Minister of Finance therefor, and that it shall pay a tax on the same as from the 16th day at a rate not less than [illegible]% p.a. The denominations of convertible notes are ¥1, ¥5, ¥10, ¥20, ¥50, ¥100 and ¥200, but in practice ¥50 and ¥200 have not been issued yet. — p. 303 ([scan part 1, leaf 362](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n362/mode/1up))

**The Yokohama Specie Bank** (Head Office—Nakaku Minami-nakadori, Yokohama.) (July to December, 1936). Established 1880. Authorized capital ¥100,000,000, which is paid up. Reserves ¥134,553,917.31, Deposits ¥553,308,607.61, Advances ¥378,758,413.60 (inclusive of bills discounted), Foreign Bills of Exchange bought ¥1,930,036,454.38 and those sold ¥1,363,876,131, Note issue ¥533,949.40 in silver yen, ¥673,539.40 in silver dollars and ¥1,730.00 in taels, Divd., 10% p.a. As stated elsewhere, the Yokohama Specie Bank is engaged chiefly in the foreign exchange business. It has 41 branches and sub-branches, of which 33 are abroad. Besides many privileges granted by the Government, the Bank is authorised to issue bank notes in China and the leased territory of Kwantung Province. — p. 303 ([scan part 1, leaf 362](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n362/mode/1up))

**The Nippon Kwangyo Ginko** (Hypothec Bank of Japan) (Head Office—Marunouchi, Kojimachi, Tokyo). Established 1897. Authorized capital ¥140,920,000.00, ¥116,796,062.50 is paid up. Reserves ¥137,510,997.94, Deposits ¥272,703,658.21, Advances ¥1,309,495,243.73, Issue of Hypothec and other debentures ¥1,054,661,563.00, Divd., 10% p.a. The Nippon Kwangyo Ginko was originally intended to raise funds by issuing debentures and advance them to agriculturalists and industrialists on the security of real estate for a long time at a low rate of interest. The scope of business of the Bank has since been greatly enlarged. The Bank is authorised to issue hypothec debentures with premiums to the amount fifteen times the paid-up capital. — p. 303 ([scan part 1, leaf 362](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n362/mode/1up))

**Agricultural and Industrial Banks** The first agricultural and industrial bank was opened in Shizuoka in the same year as the Hypothec Bank of Japan, or 1897. Its original purpose was also the same as that of the Hypothec Bank, the former serving as a local organ and the latter as a central organ. There were established altogether 46 of these bank, one in each fu and ken, with the single exception of the Hokkaido, the Awa Agricultural and Industrial Bank established in August, 1900 being the last. As in the case of the Hypothec Bank of Japan the scope of business of the agricultural and industrial banks has since been much enlarged. In 1921 a law providing for the amalgamation of agricultural and industrial banks with the Hypothec Bank of Japan was promulgated. Since then twenty-seven agricultural and industrial banks have been merged in the Hypothec Bank of Japan. As at the end of 1935 there were 17 of these banks, their branch offices numbering 63. Their combined capital was ¥84,500,000.00, of which ¥77,750,000.00 was paid up, Reserves ¥70,821,000.00, approximately, Deposits ¥167,834,000.00, Advances ¥580,341,000.00, Bills discounted ¥8,131,000.00, Issue of agricultural and industrial debentures ¥429,543,000.00, Divd., ¥8,581,000.00. — p. 304 ([scan part 1, leaf 362](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n362/mode/1up))

**The Hokkaido Colonial Bank** (Head Office—Sapporo, Hokkaido). Established 1899. Authorised capital ¥20,000,000.00, ¥12,500,000.00 paid-up. Reserves ¥15,604,900.00, Deposits ¥108,993,967.327, Advances ¥141,886,882.90, Debenture issue ¥121,715,530.000, Divd., 7% p.a. It was for the purpose of financing colonial industries in the Hokkaido and Karafuto that the Bank was established towards the end of 1899. It is not much different from the Hypothec Bank of Japan and the agricultural and industrial banks in that the Bank makes loans on the security of real estate. What the Bank differs from those banks is that besides making loans on shares and debentures issued by the companies intended to promote the colonal interests of the Hokkaido and Karafuto and taking up the issue of debentures, it makes advances on the security of bills of exchange and documentary drafts and local products. The Bank is authorised to issue Hokkaido Colonial debentures to the amount not more than fifteen times the paid-up capital. — p. 304 ([scan part 1, leaf 362](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n362/mode/1up))

**The Industrial Bank of Japan** (Head Office—Marunouchi, Kojimachi, Tokyo). Established 1900. Authorised capital ¥50,000,000.00, paid-up. Reserves ¥29,615,597.50, Deposits ¥194,073,102.70, Advances ¥301,051,685.44, Industrial debenture issue ¥244,968,448.30, Divd., 6% p.a. The Industrial Bank of Japan was established in 1900 in accordance with the provisions of the Industrial Bank Act promulgated in March of that year and opened in April, 1902, its object being to finance various industries, railways and harbour construction by advancing loans on securities such as shares, debentures, etc. The scope of business of the Bank has since also been much extended. The Bank is authorised to issue Industrial debentures to the amount of not more than ten times the paid-up capital. — p. 304 ([scan part 1, leaf 362](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n362/mode/1up))

**The Bank of Taiwan** (Head Office—Sakaemachi, Taihoku, Taiwan). Established 1899. Capital authorised ¥15,000,000.00, of which ¥13,125,000,000 is paid-up. Reserves, ¥5,700,000.00, Deposits ¥140,193,261.26, Advances ¥68,819,781.24, Foreign Bills of Exchange bought ¥581,616,414.39 and those sold ¥250,13,323.39, Note issue ¥75,489,725.50, Divd., 3% p.a. The Bank was established for the purpose of opening up the resources of Taiwan by financing commerce and industry and public enterprises as a central organ for monetary circulation in the island and also extending the scope of its business to South China and the South Seas, thereby serving as an organ of trade between the island and those countries. The Bank has extended the scope of its business not only to South China and the South Seas but also to Europe and America. It is authorised to issue bank notes. — p. 304 ([scan part 1, leaf 362](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n362/mode/1up))

**The Bank of Chosen** (Head Office—Nandaimon-dori, Keijo, Chosen). Established 1909. Capital authorised ¥40,000,000.000, of which ¥25,000,000.000 is paid-up. Reserves ¥8,101,026,570, Deposits ¥291,338,522.719, Advances ¥399,200,062.770, Divd., 4% p.a. The Bank of Chosen not only serves as the central organ for monetary circulation for the peninsula but also finances trade between Japan proper and Korea and Manchoukuo. Another notable feature of the business of the Bank is the foreign exchange business which it has dealt with since it opened a foreign exchange account in 1916. It has extended its activity to the exchange market in London and New York. — p. 304 ([scan part 1, leaf 362](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n362/mode/1up))

## Manchoukuo — Banking: Japanese and Chinese banks

### Japanese Banks

**Oriental Development Co** The Government also commissioned the Oriental Development Company which entered the field of Manchuria to undertake the task of providing funds required for real estate deals. As a result, the Yokohame Specie Bank was obliged to return to its original field of an exchange bank. Thus, the Yokohama Specie Bank, the Bank of Chosen and the Oriental Development Company have become the three main Japanese banking organizations in Manchuria in their respective fields of activity. — p. 736 ([scan part 1, leaf 801](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n801/mode/1up))

### Chinese Banks

**Bank of China** The Bank of China was established in 1911 with a capital of 25,000,000 yuan, of which 24,712,200 yuan is paid up. It is the first class bank in China. The Head Office is in Shanghai. Originally it was known as the Huipu Bank Bank which was established in 1908 with a capital of Tls. 10,000,000. Later it was renamed as the Taching Bank. It was after China became a republic and the bank was again renamed the Bank of China that it extended its activity to Manchuria. Its first branch was established in Changchun in 1913. In 1927 it was removed to Harbin in order to meet the growing economic activity in that place.. Prior to this, or in 1919 a branch office was opened in Mukden. Thus, the Bank of China exerted influence over both North and South Manchuria. The situation has changed since the foundation of Manchoukuo. In 1935 in Hsinking there was established the Manchou Headquarters of the Central Bank of China. Although the Bank has many branches and sub-branches with Mukden and Harbin as the centre, it wields no such influence as it once enjoyed together with the former government banks and the frontier banks. Since the independence of Manchoukuo, the Bank has lost the privilege of dealing with public money and of issuing notes, and with the growing credit of the Central Bank of Manchou, it has gradually lost its hold on the exchange business. — p. 737 ([scan part 1, leaf 801](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n801/mode/1up))

**Bank of Communications** The Bank of Communications was founded in 1907 as a direct organ of the quondam Post and Telegraph Department of China with the object of promoting the railway, steamship, postal and telegraph services. The authorized capital is 10,000,000 yuan, of which 8,715,600 yuan was paid up. It is one of the two largest special banks of China, the other being the Bank of China. The Bank extended its activity to Manchuria in June, 1908 when it established a branch office at Yingkow. Later branches were opened in Changchun and Mukden. After the inauguration of the Republican regime other branches were set up in Harbin, Kirin and Heilungkiang. At present the branch office is in Hsinking and sub-branches are in Harbin, Kirin, Tsitsihar, Mukden and Yingkow. Harbin and Mukden are still the centre of the activity of the Bank. — p. 737 ([scan part 1, leaf 801](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n801/mode/1up))

**Chingcheng Bank** The Chingcheng Bank was established in May, 1917 with a capital of 10,000,000 yuan, of which 7,000,000 yuan is paid-up. The Head Office is in Shanghai. The Harbin branch was set up in May, 1931. There is also a branch in Dairen. — p. 737 ([scan part 1, leaf 801](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n801/mode/1up))

**Tachung Bank** The Tachung Bank was brought into being in March, 1929 with a capital of 4,000,000 yuan, of which 2,600,000 yuan is paid-up. Its Manchu branch is at Harbin. — p. 737 ([scan part 1, leaf 801](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n801/mode/1up))

**Tunglai Bank** The Bank is capitalized at 3,000,000 yuan and has its Head Office at Tientsin and a branch at Dairen. — p. 737 ([scan part 1, leaf 801](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n801/mode/1up))


## Manchoukuo — Banking: Other foreign banks

### Other Foreign Banks

**Huifeng Bank** The Huifeng Bank, which is an English bank commonly known as the Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corporation, was established in Honkong in 1865 with a capital of 50,000,000 Chinese dollars, of which 20,000,000 dollars is paid up. It shows great activity as an issuing and exchange bank, in South and Central China with Honkong as the centre. With the declining of the activity of Russian banks in North Manchuria, the Bank extended its activity to Harbin. It has branches in Harbin, Mukden and Dairen. It is engaged chiefly in financing industries and the import trade in miscellaneous goods. — p. 738 ([scan part 1, leaf 803](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n803/mode/1up))

**Huachi Bank** The Huachi Bank, an American bank, was established in 1901. In 1926 it was merged in the National City Bank of New York (established in 1812). It is capitalized at $127,500,000 and has reserves for $130,000,000, approximattely. It has branches in Harbin and Dairen. The Bank's advances in Manchoukuo have so far been limited to leading American and European business men and a portion of Manchou capitalists. — p. 738 ([scan part 1, leaf 803](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n803/mode/1up))

**Maichiali Bank** The Maichiali Bank is an English bank. It is widely known as the Chartered Bank and has its head office at London. It is capitalized at £3,000,000. It was in 1928 that the Bank extended its activity to Manchuria. It has a branch office at Harbin. — p. 738 ([scan part 1, leaf 803](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n803/mode/1up))

**Faa Bank** The Bank known at the Banque Franco-Asiatique was established in 1829 in Paris. The authorized capital is 25,000,000 francs. It is surmised that 6,900,000 francs is paid up. It has branch offices at Harbin and Mukden. — p. 738 ([scan part 1, leaf 803](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n803/mode/1up))

**BAN, Kaoru 坂薫** Mng.-Dir. Tokyo Stock Exchange since 1936; b. Nov. 1895, Aichi-ken; s. of Keitaro Ban. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1919; entered Com. & Ind. Dept.; Commr. Patents Bureau; Chief Mining Adm. Sec. Osaka Mining Supt. Bureau; Commr. Com. & Ind. Dept.; Chief Exchange Sec. Com. Bureau, same; Ind. Adm. Sec., Ind. Bureau; Statistics Sec.; despatched to Europe & Amer. 1935. Address: 21 Shoto-machi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo. — p. 969 ([scan part 1, leaf 1034](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1034/mode/1up))

**BARTH, Johannes** Merchant; b. 1891, Bremen, Germany. Career: came to Japan 1914; established own business 1921; at present, agent in Japan for several European industrial firms; wrote many essays in the Mitteilungen der Deutschen Gesselschaft fuer Natur und Voelkelkunde Ostasiens, of which he is Vice-President; Secretary of German Chamber of Com. in Japan; Mem. of Asiatic Soc. of Japan. Business Office: Takiyama Bldg. Nishi-Ginza 6-chome, Tokyo. Private Address: 3 Kami-Ogikubo 1-chome, Suginami-ku, Tokyo. — p. 969 ([scan part 1, leaf 1034](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1034/mode/1up))

**BASLER, Rolf W** Hotel Manager (Adviser for modern hotels in Japan); b. Aug. 1911 in Switzerland; s. of Rudolf Basler, bank mgr. Career: Attended special hotel schools in Switzerland and Mercantile School in London; thorough training in Swiss hotels as cook, waiter, reception clerk, administration, etc.; Lieut.-Quartermaster, Swiss Army. In Japan since 1934. Address: Kawana Hotel, Izu. — p. 969 ([scan part 1, leaf 1034](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1034/mode/1up))

**BASSOMPIERRE, Albert Marie Leon Adolphe de** Baron; Belgian Ambassador to Japan; b. Aug. 1873. Brussels; s. of Ernst de Bassompierre, Commr. General, Belgian Army; m. Hélenè de Woot de Trixhe. Career: Dr. Juris. Louvain Univ. 1896; later entered diplomatic service. Address: Belgian Embassy, 33 Shimo-Niban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo — p. 969 ([scan part 1, leaf 1034](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1034/mode/1up))

**BATY, Thomas** D.C.L.; LL.D.; Legal Adviser, Japanese Foreign Office; b. Feb. 1869, Cumberland, Great Britain; n. British; s. of William-Thomas Baty. Career: grad. Queens' Coll. Oxford; Trin. Coll. Cambridge; English Bar (Inner Temple) 1898; Fellow, Univ. Coll. Oxford 1895-1902; Whewell Scholar, Univ. of Cambridge 1893; Hon. Secr.-Gen. Int'l Law Assn. 1905-1916; organized conferences at Christiania, Berlin, Portland (Me.), Budapest, London, Paris and Madrid; Associate, Institut de Droit Int'l and Academic Diplomatique; former Examiner, Oxford, Liverpool, Manchester, London and Hongkong Univs. Publications: "Int'l Law," "Canons of Int'l Law," "Polarized Law," "Victorious Liability," etc. Address: 9 Urakasumigaseki, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 969 ([scan part 1, leaf 1034](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1034/mode/1up))

**BENNETT, Walter George** British Consular Agent; b. July 1867, London; n. British; s. of Edmund Hellyer Bennett. Career: grad. Aske's Hatcham Sch. Surrey, England; arrived at Nagasaki from London in 1887 and joined Holme, Ringer & Co. as Shipping Clerk; established Holme, Ringer & Co. at Jinsen, Oct. 1896 and remained as Mgr. until 1904; established Bennett & Co. 1904. Address: British Consulate, Jinsen, Chosen. — p. 969 ([scan part 1, leaf 1034](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1034/mode/1up))

**BENSCHOTEN, Arnold van** B.S.; American Vice-Consul at Dairen since 1931; b. May 1905, Providence R.I., U.S.A.; s. of G. W. Van Benschoten, doctor. Career: grad. Dartmouth Coll. 1928, Harvard Univ. 1928-29; Vice-Consul, Halifax, Canada 1930; studied at Foreign Service Officers' Training Sch. Washington 1931. Address: American Consulate, Dairen. — p. 970 ([scan part 1, leaf 1035](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1035/mode/1up))

**BERLAS, N. H** B.A. (Allahabad Univ.), B.T. (Aligarh Univ.), Lecturer Tokyo Sch. of Foreign Languages; b. June 1890, Delhi, India; s. of M. T. Berlas, educator; m. A. J. Berlas. Career: taught at several High Schools in India for 20 yrs.; was Dir. of 2 of them; lectured Hindustani in Tokyo Sch. of Foreign Lang. 4 yrs.; Hon. Secr. Red Cross Soc. and St. John's Ambulance Assn. of a local branch 4 yrs.; is a student of Islam and of Japanese culture; contributor to Indian periodicals on the subjects about Japan to enlighten people of his native land. Address: 790 Togoshi-machi, Ebara-ku, Tokyo. — p. 970 ([scan part 1, leaf 1035](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1035/mode/1up))

**BERRICK, Bertram, R** Hon. Consul for Finland; b. July 1878, London; s. of Lester Berrick, merchant; m. Gertrude Mendelson. Career: educated Townley Castle Sch. and continent; came to Japan Nov. 1898; joined Berrick Bros. Yokohama. Address: 199 Yamashita-cho, Yokohama. — p. 970 ([scan part 1, leaf 1035](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1035/mode/1up))

**BERRY, Arthur D** D.D.; Missionary; b. Mexico, New York, U.S.A. Address: Aoyama Gakuin, Aoyama, Tokyo. — p. 970 ([scan part 1, leaf 1035](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1035/mode/1up))

**BETSUMIYA, Hideo 別宮秀夫** Vice-Governor, Antung Prov.; b. Nov. 1887, Ehime-ken; s. of Ranzo Betsumiya. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1913; Police Chief, Yamagata-ken, Fukushima-ken, Wakayama-ken, Hokkaido & Aichi-ken; Chief, Home Dept. Miye-ken & Kumamoto-ken. Address: c/o Antung Prov. Office, Antung. — p. 970 ([scan part 1, leaf 1035](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1035/mode/1up))

**BISCHOFF, Ernest** Dr. phil.; German Consul at Dairen since 1935; b. July 1880, Muenchen; s. of Theodor Bischoff, director of a railway company; m. Hertha Bischoff, née Zelle. Career: Counsellor of Legation at German Embassy Tokyo 1925-26; Consul at Kobe 1926-34. Address: c/o German Consulate, Dairen. — p. 970 ([scan part 1, leaf 1035](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1035/mode/1up))

**BOCHIA, A. M. M** Mgr. Eastern Export Co. at Kobe; b. 1913, Rangoon, Burma. Address: 11 Isogami-dori 7-chome, Kobe. — p. 970 ([scan part 1, leaf 1035](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1035/mode/1up))

**BOKU, Ei-ko 朴泳孝** Marquis (cr. 1910); Mem. House of Peers; Adviser, Board of Councillors, Chosen Govt.-Gen.; Pres. Keijo Spinning Co.; Dir. Chosen Land Improvement Co.; b. June 1861, Bannan, Suigen District, Keiki-do. Career: held important positions in political circles in Chosen since 1892; nominated Peer 1933. Address: 81 Suijin-do, Keijo. — p. 970 ([scan part 1, leaf 1035](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1035/mode/1up))

**BOKU, Ei-tetsu 朴榮喆** Mem. Board of Councillors, Chosen Govt.; Pres. Chosen Com. Bank; Spec. Mem. Keijo Chamber of Com. & Ind.; b. Feb. 1879, Zenshu; s. of Boku Ki-jun. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1903; Gov. Kogendo and Kita-Kankyodo; Inspector, Oriental Development Co.; Pres. Sannan Bank 1927; Vice-Pres. of present bank 1928; Pres. 1931. Address: 144 Shokakudo, Keijo. — p. 970 ([scan part 1, leaf 1035](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1035/mode/1up))

**BOKU, Shun-kin 朴春琴** Pres. Soai-kai; Mng.-Dir. Nissen Enterprise Co.; Prop. Nissen Kaikan; b. Apr. 1891, Keisho Nando, Chosen. Career: grad. Mitsuyo Kanbun Shojuku (Chinese Classics Sch.); Nichigo Gakko (Japanese Language Sch.); founded Sokyu-kai (Mutual Relief Society), Soai-kai (Mutual Friendship Society); went to Manchuria and Mongolia to inspect condition of Chosenese; sent to Diet from Tokyo 1932. Address: 1 Umayabashi, Honjo-ku, Tokyo. — p. 970 ([scan part 1, leaf 1035](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1035/mode/1up))

**BOPP, Raul** Brazilian Consul at Yokohama; b. Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, 1898. Career: grad. Law Coll. Univ. of Rio de Janeiro. Address: 1,500 Araijuku 2-chome, Omori-ku, Tokyo. Tel. Omori 1123. — p. 970 ([scan part 1, leaf 1035](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1035/mode/1up))

**BOSE, Rash Behari** Journalist; Lecturer; Corr. of Indian Papers; Editor of "New Asia," a monthly paper standing for Complete Independence of Asia; b. Mar. 1886, Bengal, India; n. Indian; Naturalized as Japanese citizen, 1923; s. of Benode Behari Bose, official. Career: grad. Dupleix Coll., French Chandernagore; Morton Inst., Calcutta, India; worked as Chief Clerk, Forest Research Institute, Indian Govt.; joined Indian Govt.; joined Indian Independence Agitation and led revolutionary movement in India 1910-15; was charged by the Indian Govt. with sedition, conspiracy to wage war against the British King, creating disaffection among Indian soldiers for revolutionary purposes, throwing bomb upon and severely injuring Lord Hardinge, Viceroy of India, and a reward of twelve thousand Rupees was announced for his arrest; fled from India as refugee after unsuccessful uprising in 1915 to Japan, where he was ordered to be deported by Japanese Govt., but rescued and protected by Mitsuru Toyama, later Premier Inukai and other Japanese political leaders, and naturalized as Japanese Citizen; is active in Japan for Indian Independence, Asiatic Renaissance and World Peace based on justice and love; built "Asia Lodge," dormitory for Indian and other South Asiatic students, at 401 Yodobashi-machi, Tokyo; published the following books (in Japanese); Prospect of Revolutionary Asia, pages 325; Indian Tales of Wits, pages 340; India in Revolution, pages 428; India in Bondage, pages [?]; Indian Folk Tales, pages 272; Victory of Young Asia, pages 245. Address: 79 Onden 3-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo. — p. 970 ([scan part 1, leaf 1035](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1035/mode/1up))

**BOWLES, Gilbert** M.A.; LL.D.; Missionary; Chairman Board of Trustees, Friends Girls' Sch.; Sch. of Japanese Language and Culture; b. Oct. 1869, Stuart, Iowa; U.S.A.; s. of Ephraim Bowles; m. Teacher in Kansas Public Sch.; same, Indian Sch., Tunesassa, New York; same in Penn. Coll., Oskaloosa, Iowa; missionary in Tokyo since Feb. 1901; representing Soc. of Friends, Philadelphia. Address: 14 Mita Daimachi 1-chome, Shiba-ku, Tokyo. — p. 970 ([scan part 1, leaf 1035](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1035/mode/1up))

**BRICENO, Julio E** Consul-Gen. for Panama at Yokohama & Tokyo since 1931; b. Feb. 14, 1910, Panama City; s. of Alejandro Briceno, judge, public notary, diplomat; m. Beatrice Schnahenbeck 1931; profession journalist; consular official. Career; Reporter "Panama-America," "Diario de Panama," "Grafico" and "Accion Comual," 1928-31; served Immigration Dept, Panama Foreign Office 1930; Secr. to Premier Vallarino 1931; Chief of 1st Sec., Dept. of Govt. & Justice 1931; since Mar. 20, 1931 Consul at Yokohama. Address: Panama Consulate, 157 Yamashita-cho, Naka-ku, Yokohama. — p. 970 ([scan part 1, leaf 1035](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1035/mode/1up))

**BRUCE, Robert Randolph** Hon., B.Sc., C.E., F.R.G.S., LL.D.; Canadian Minister to Tokyo since 1936; b. July 1863 at St. Andrew's, Lhanbryd, Elgin; s. of Rev. Charles Bruce, M.A.; m. 1st, Lady Elizabeth Northcote (deceased), y. d. of 2nd Earl of Iddlesleigh; 2nd. Edith Badgley, d. of late W. A. Molson, M.D., widow of Richard Benedict Van Horne, 1932. Educ.: The Gymnasium, Old Aberdeen; Glasgow Univ. Career: Scientific Staff, Wm. Denny & Bros., Dumbarton, 1883-87; went to Canada 1887; Eng. Staff, C. P. Railway, 1887-95; engaged in mining, British Columbia, 1887-97; Pres. Mine Owners' Assn. of the Interior, 1923-25; Lieut.-Gov., British Columbia, 1926-31; Dir., Consolidated Mining & Smelting Co. of Canada. Address: Canadian Legation, 16 Omote-cho, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo. — p. 971 ([scan part 1, leaf 1036](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1036/mode/1up))

**BRUMBAUGH, Thoburn Taylor** Methodist Missionary; b. Aug. 1896, Agosta, Ohio; s. of Rev. E. G. Brumbaugh, Methodist Minister. Career: grad. Oberlin Business Coll. Ohio 1914; Army service, U. S. A. and in France 1917-19; Ohio Wesleyan Univ. Delaware 1920 (B.A.); Sch. of Theol. Boston Univ. 1924 (S.T.B.); Union Theol. Sem. New York 1930 (S.T.M.); Methodist Student Pastor, Harvard Univ. 1923-24; Asst. Pastor, Grace Methodist Church, Dayton, Ohio 1922-23; Missionary in Japan since 1924. Publications: "Religious Values in Japanese Culture." Address: 65 Miyashita-cho, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo. — p. 971 ([scan part 1, leaf 1036](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1036/mode/1up))

**BRUNER, Glen Willard** B.S. (Colo. Agr. Col.); M.A. (Northwestern Univ.); Amer. Vice Consul at Nagasaki; b. Aug. 1897, Red Cloud, Nebr., U.S.A.; s. of Chas. S. Bruner. Career: U. S. Reclamation Service 1917; U. S. Army 1917-19; Teacher of Science Eaton High Sch. Colorado 1919-20; educ. work in Japan 1920-31; service at present office since 1931. Address: Amer. Consulate Nagasaki. — p. 971 ([scan part 1, leaf 1036](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1036/mode/1up))

**BUCHANAN, Daniel Crump** B.A.; M.A.; B.D.; Ph.D.; Missionary of Presbyterian Church in U.S.A.; engaged in Newspaper Evangelism; b. June 1892, Kobe; s. of Dr. William C. Buchanan, missionary for 44 years in Japan; m. Katharine Baetjer. Career: grad. Fredericksburg Coll. 1912; Washington and Lee Univs. 1914; Presb. Theol. Sem. Chicago 1921; Hartford Sem. Foundation 1934; taught in Hagi Middle Sch. Yamaguchi-ken 1914-16; Yamaguchi Middle Sch. and Yamaguchi Higher Com. Sch. 1916-17; Kwansai Gakuin 1917-18; went to U. Address: Ichijo-dori, Muro-machi Nishi, Kyoto. — p. 971 ([scan part 1, leaf 1036](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1036/mode/1up))

**CANALI, Lionel** Hon. Consul for Japan at Genoa; b. Mar. 1890, Genoa: s. of late Edward Canali. Address: Via Lomellino, 8, Genoa, Italy. — p. 971 ([scan part 1, leaf 1036](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1036/mode/1up))

**CATTO, Alexander Ross** Cable Corr. & Ins. Agent since 1928; b. Oct. 1867, London; s. of John Catto; n. Scottish. Career: grad. St. Saviour's Coll. **CHAMBERLIN, William Henry** A. B. (Haverford Coll.); Writer & Journalist; b. Feb. 1897, Brooklyn, New York; s. of Ernest V. Chamberlin; m. Sophie Trosten. Career: grad. William Penn Charter Sch. **CHAPMAN, James Jeffries** D.D.; Clergyman; b. July 1873, Fauquier County, Virginia, U. S. A.; s. of William Henry Chapman, govt. official; m. Ellen Ritchie Scott. Career: missionary of Amer. Epis. Church in Kyoto Diocese since 1899. Address: Karasumaru, Shimotachiuri-agaru, Kyoto. — p. 972 ([scan part 1, leaf 1037](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1037/mode/1up))

**CHENG Hsiao-hsu 鄭孝胥** Ex-Prime Minister of Manchoukuo; b. 1859, Foochow, China. Career: Consul at Kobe; resided in Lungchow as Kwangsi Frontier Defence Min.; apptd. Inspector-Gen. Kwantung & Anhui Prov. 1907; engaged in business at Shanghai; founded Const. Govt. Prep. Soc. to advocate Const. Govt.; Inspector, Construction of China Ry. & Lienshan Bay Harbor, under Gov.-Gen. Three Eastern Prov. 1909; Gov. Hunan Prov.; Dir. Shanghai Com. Press; Dir. Shanghai Savings Bk.; attended present Manchou Emperor when he was in Tientsin; exerted in establishment of Manchoukuo; Prime Minister & Educ. Min. 1932-35; visited Japan as Spec. Envoy 1934. Address: Hsinking. — p. 972 ([scan part 1, leaf 1037](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1037/mode/1up))

**CHENG Lin-kao 鄭林皐** Sch. Inspector, Manchoukuo People's Welfare Dept.; b. May 1883 Suihua-hsien, Heilungkiang Prov.; s. of Cheng I-ling, businessman. Career: Pres. North East Univ. of Communications 1927; Govt. Committee, Heilungkiang Prov. 1930; Chief, Educ. Dept. same; Commr. Heilungkiang Prov. Office, and Chief, Educ. Dept. of same, 1932. Address: c/o People's Welfare Dept. Hsinking. — p. 972 ([scan part 1, leaf 1037](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1037/mode/1up))

**CHENG Yu 鄭禹** Postal Adm. Bureau of Manchoukuo; b. 1889, Foochow, China; s. of Cheng Hsiao-Hsu, ex-prime Minister. Career: studied at Seijo Sch. Tokyo 1905; grad. Liverpool Univ. 1911; Manager, Kinghua Publishing Co. Peking 1919; Mgr. Tungchi Printing Office, Mukden 1922; Mgr. South Branch, Chihsin Cement Co. Shanghai 1927; Mng.-Dir. Huafeng Enamel Co. Shanghai 1930; Secr. to Prime Min. 1932; Dir. Cap. Constr. Bureau 1935-37. Address: Postal Adm. Bureau, Hsinking. — p. 972 ([scan part 1, leaf 1037](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1037/mode/1up))

**CHI Pin 啓彬** Aud. Ind. Bank of Manchou since Dec. 1936; b. 1887, Shengyang-hsien, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Waseda Univ. Tokyo; Magistrate Changchun-hsien, Kirin Prov.; Adviser to Gov. Kirin Prov.; Chief, Yenki Muni. System Adm. Planning Office, Kirin; Dir. Revenue Supt. Bureau Mukden 1932-36. Address: 202 Daido-Daigai, Hsinking. — p. 972 ([scan part 1, leaf 1037](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1037/mode/1up))

**CHIANG Chun 江濬** Councillor & Vice-Chief of Harbin Ry. Factory of S.M.R.; b. Feb. 1900 Shanghai; s. of Chiang Shih-tsuan, Admiral of Changkiang Fleet in Ching Dynasty. Career: Chief Engr., Mukden Arsenal; taught Aviation Sch.; Chief Instructor, Harbin Higher Engrg. Sch.; Prof. Harbin Engrg. Coll.; Sec. Chief, Engrg. Affairs, Chinese Eastern Ry.; Vice-Chief, Head Factory same. Address: 83 Shoshigai-dori, Harbin, Manchoukuo. — p. 972 ([scan part 1, leaf 1037](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1037/mode/1up))

**CHIANG En-chi 蔣恩之** Dir. Gen. Monopoly Bureau of Manchoukuo; b. 1899, Yushou-hsien, Kirin Prov. Career: grad. Polit. & Econ. Dept. Chaoyang Univ. Peiping; Magistrate, Mengkiang, Huatien and Yushouhsiens, Kirin Prov. Address: Gen. Monopoly Bureau, Hsinking. — p. 972 ([scan part 1, leaf 1037](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1037/mode/1up))

**CHI-MO-TE-SE-MU-PEI-LO 齊默特色木丕勒** Manchoukuo Privy Councillor; b. Feb. 1891, Kuoerhissuchien Banner. Career: Prince Hoshih, Chelimu League 1902; Mem. House of Commons 1922; Mem. Constitution Draft Committee; Gov. Hsingan Adm. Office 1932-34; Min. of Mongolia Adm. 1934-37. **CHIN Hsien-li 金憲立** Mayor of Tsitsihar since 1932. Career: grad. Tung Wen Coll. Shanghai; studied in Tokyo; apptd. Foreign Affairs Secr., Heilungkiang Prov. Address: Tsitsihar Muni. Office, Tsitsihar. — p. 973 ([scan part 1, leaf 1038](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1038/mode/1up))

**CHIN Jung-kei 金榮桂** Mayor of Mukden; b. 1877, Kaiping-hsein, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Peking Coll. 1909; Gen. Dir. Tsinan Muni. Office; Chief Police Gen. Adm. Office, Tung Sheng Spec. District; Dir. Chinese Eastern Ry. (North Manchuria Ry.) 1932; Police Chief Harbin 1933-35; Metro. Police Chief 1936-37. Address: Muni. Office, Mukden. — p. 973 ([scan part 1, leaf 1038](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1038/mode/1up))

**CHING Min-shih 金名世** Gov. Jehol Prov. since 1937; b. 1896, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Law Coll. Peiping; Secr. Kirin Prov. Office; Dir. Harbin Elec. Bureau; Chief Police Dept. Kirin Prov. 1933-34; Gov. Sankiang Prov. Address: Governor's Residence, Chengteh. — p. 973 ([scan part 1, leaf 1038](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1038/mode/1up))

**CHINO, Gitaro (Shosho) 茅野儀太郎** Prof. of German Litt. Keio Univ.; Poet; b. Mar. 1883, Nagano-ken; s. of Naotaro Chino. Career: grad. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908; Prof. 3rd Higher Sch.; Prof. Nihon Women's Univ. Address: 1071 Nakanobu-machi, Ebara-ku, Tokyo. — p. 973 ([scan part 1, leaf 1038](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1038/mode/1up))

**CHIWAKI, Morinosuke 血脇守之助** LL.D. (America); Dentist; Pres. Tokyo Dental Coll.; Japan Dental Assn.; b. Feb. 1870, Chiba-ken; s. of Seinosuke Kato. Career: grad. Keio Univ.; studied at Takayama Dental Inst.; became Corr. Tokyo Shimpo; Teacher of English of middle sch.; Secr. and Lecturer, Takayama Dental Inst.; founded Tokyo Dental Inst. (now Tokyo Dental Coll.) 1900; founded Japan Dental Assn. 1903; author of books on dental science. Address: 496 Sendagaya 3-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo. — p. 973 ([scan part 1, leaf 1038](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1038/mode/1up))

**CHO, Shun-ichi 長俊一** Dir. Hiroshima Higher Tech. Sch.; b. Dec. 1881, Yonezawa; s. of Shimizu Cho; m. Maki, d. of Kichihei Suzuki. Career: grad. Sc. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1906; apptd. Prof. Hiroshima Higher Normal Sch. 1908; Yokohama Higher Tech. Sch. 1920; went to U. S. A., Germany & France for study; Sch-Inspector Dept. of Educ. 1927; Dir. Hamamatsu Higher Tech. Sch. 1932-36. Address: c/o Hiroshima Higher Tech. Sch., Hiroshima. — p. 973 ([scan part 1, leaf 1038](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1038/mode/1up))

**CHRISTIANS, Jann** Chancellor; b. Jan. 1884, Germany; m. Paula Dierks. Career: Consular Service since 1905, mostly in the Far East and Japan. Address: German Consulate, 51-B Yamashita-cho, Yokohama. — p. 973 ([scan part 1, leaf 1038](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1038/mode/1up))

**CHU Chih-cheng 朱之正** b. 1893, Kiangsu Prov. Career: Gov. Lingnan-Tao, Kwantung Prov. Councillor Home Dept. & Staff Officer, Kwantung & Kwangsi Inspector-Gen.'s Office in China Dynasty; Dir. Gen. Affairs Bureau, Manchoukuo Foreign Dept. Address: Hsinking. — p. 973 ([scan part 1, leaf 1038](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1038/mode/1up))

**CHUO-LA-BA-TUR 綽羅巴圖爾** Major-Gen.; Comdr. Hsingan East Prov. Guards Army; b. 1902, Mongolia. Career: grad. Hwangpu Mil. Coll. Shiangsu Prov.; studied in Tokyo; Comdr. Mongolia Self Defence Army 1931; Comdr. Hsingan East Sub-prov. Peace Preservation Corps 1932; Chief Staff & Acting Comdr. Hsingan East Prov. Guards Army, 1933. Address: Hsingan East Prov. Guards Army Hdqrs., Pukotu, Manchoukuo. — p. 973 ([scan part 1, leaf 1038](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1038/mode/1up))

**COBB, John B** B.A.; M.A.; Missionary; b. Oct. 1893, Macon, Georgia, U.S.A.; s. of James Jackson Cobb, banker; m. Theodora Cook Atkinson. Career: Prof. at Kentucky Wesleyan Coll. 1915-17; came to Japan 1918; taught at Palmore Institute, Kobe 1919-27 and 1932-33; Evangelistic Work and Principal of Fraser Institute, Hiroshima 1927-31; Principal, Osaka English Sch. since 1933. Address: Eki Kita, Ashiya, Hyogo-ken. — p. 973 ([scan part 1, leaf 1038](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1038/mode/1up))

**CONRADY, Alexander** Dr. phli.; Prof. and Writer; b. Aug. 1875, Bursheid near Cologne, Germany; s. of Edmund Conrady; m. Marie Berg. Career: studied history, polit. econ. and phil. in Bonn, Berlin, Leipzig Univs. 1893-97; Dr. phil. Address: c/o Kochi Koto Gakko, Kochi City. — p. 973 ([scan part 1, leaf 1038](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1038/mode/1up))

**COOTE, Leonard W** Missionary; b. Apr. 1890, Enfield, Middlesex, England; s. of Ernest Coote; m. Esther Keene. Address: P. O. Box 5, Ikoma, Nara-ken. — p. 973 ([scan part 1, leaf 1038](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1038/mode/1up))

**CORDING, Hans** Rep. Dir. Dai-Nippon Kali Kaisha. Career: engaged in different kinds of business in London. Africa, Singapore, Java, China; in Japan since 1929. Address: (office) Teikoku Seimei Bldg., Marunouchi, Tokyo. — p. 973 ([scan part 1, leaf 1038](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1038/mode/1up))

**COVILLE, Cabot** A.B. 2nd Secr. American Embassy in Tokyo since 1935; b. Mar. 1902, Washington, D.C.; s. of Dr. Frederick V. Coville, botanist; m. Lilian Grosvenor. Career: grad. Cornell Univ. 1923; entered U. S. foreign service 1926; attache embassy Tokyo 1927-29, vice-consul Kobe 1930; consul Dairen 1930-31, Kobe 1931, Tokyo 1932, Harbin 1932-34; Dept. of State, Washington D. C. 1935. Address: American Embassy, Tokyo. — p. 973 ([scan part 1, leaf 1038](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1038/mode/1up))

**COX, Melville James** Journalist; b. Dec. 1885, London; s. of Herbert Robert Cox, company secretary. Career: joined Reuter's London Office 1901; proceeded Bombay 1907; Mgr. Reuter's Colombo Office 1909-11; Mgr. Reuter's Shanghai Office 1912-19; Mgr. Reuter's Far Eastern News Service 1925-33; Reuter's Chief Corr. in Japan since 1934. Address: Reuters Ltd., 9 Ginza Nishi 8-chome, Kyobashi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 973 ([scan part 1, leaf 1038](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1038/mode/1up))

**CURTIS, John L** A.B.; Supervisor, Japan and Manchoukuo Branches of The National City Bank of N. Y.; b. in Camden, Maine, U. S. A.; s. of John C. Curtis. Career: grad. New York Office 1931-32; present post since 1933. Address: c/o The National City Bank of New York, Marunouchi, Tokyo. — p. 973 ([scan part 1, leaf 1038](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1038/mode/1up))

**CUTSEM, Alphonse van** Consul-General & Acting Minister for Belgium at Shanghai; b. Sept. 1883, Antwerp. Career: Cons.-Gen. at Harbin; transferred to Shanghai 1927. **DAN, Ino 團伊能** Baron; Dir. Society for Int. Cultural Relations; b. Feb. 1892, Omuta City; s. of late Baron Takuma Dan; m. Michiko, d. of Suesaburo Ueno. Career: grad. Litt. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Prof. 1927; sent to China 1931; resigned 1933; succeeded peerage 1932; decorated with Commander le Crown by Italian Emperor 1929. Address: 344 Harajuku 3-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo. — p. 974 ([scan part 1, leaf 1039](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1039/mode/1up))

**DANNO, Reisuke 檀野禮助** Dir. Hokkaido Colliery & Steamship Co., Yubari Ry. Co.; b. Aug. 1875, Nagasaki-ken; s. of Katsuji Danno. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; visited Europe & Amer. and attended Int'l Rotarian Assembly at Denver as Japanese Delegate 1926; sent to Diet 1928. Address: 89 Myogadani-machi, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo. — p. 974 ([scan part 1, leaf 1039](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1039/mode/1up))

**DAS, Susil Chandra** Merchant; Hon. Treasurer, Indian Trade Assn. at Kobe; b. Aug. 1888, Calcutta. Career: came to Japan 1915; Pres. Indian Club 1921-29; elected its Hon. **D'ECKHOUTTE, Maurice Iweins** D.L.; Secr. of Emb.; b. Dec. 1904, Ypres, Belgium; s. of Henri Iweins d'Eeckhoutte; m. Zosia Wroblewska. **DOIHARA, Kenji 土肥原賢二** Lieut.-Gen.; Comdr. 14th Division since Mar. 1937; b. 1883, Okayama-ken. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1905; grad. Mil. Staff Coll.; Staff, Gen. Staff Office, Comdr. Address: 21 Shimizu-dori, Komegafukuro, Sendai. — p. 986 ([scan part 1, leaf 1051](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1051/mode/1up))

**HONDA, Kumataro 本多熊太郎** Writer; b. Dec. 1874, Wakayama-ken; s. of Uhei Honda. Career: grad. Tokyo Senmon Gakko and Hogakuin and later Univ. of Brussels; Secr. to Foreign Minister; Secr. Legation and Embassy; Counsellor of Emb. in London during world War; Minister to Switzerland and Austria; Amb. to Germany 1923-26. Address: 1080 Kamimeguro 7-chome, Meguroku, Tokyo. — p. 986 ([scan part 1, leaf 1051](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1051/mode/1up))

**HONDA, Seiroku 本多靜六** Dr. of Forestry; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Pres. Teikoku Shinrin-kai; b. July 1866, Saitama-ken. Career: grad. Agrl. Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1890; studied at Munchen Univ (D. Econ.) 1892; rec'd deg. 1899; Prof. Agrl. Coll Tokyo Imp Univ. 1900-27; went to Siberia, China, and Chosen 1902; Philippine, Australia, and South China 1903; Europe & Africa 1907; West Indies and Siam 1913; South Africa & South America 1921. Address: 95 Sakuragaoka-machi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo. — p. 986 ([scan part 1, leaf 1051](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1051/mode/1up))

**HONJO, Shigeru 本庄繁** General on the reserve list; Former Chief Aide-de-camp to the Emperor. (See 1936 issue.) — p. 986 ([scan part 1, leaf 1051](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1051/mode/1up))

**HOOPS, Walther Dietrich** Dr. phil.; Vice-Consul at German Consulate-General in Osaka & Kobe; b. Aug. 1900, Heidelberg; s. of Prof. Johannes Hoops. Career: Ph. D. Address: 32/39 Yamamoto-dori 2-chome, Kobe. — p. 986 ([scan part 1, leaf 1051](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1051/mode/1up))

Address: 476 Yoyogi Hatsudai, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo. — p. 986 ([scan part 1, leaf 1051](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1051/mode/1up))

Sch. 1904; joined Osaka Shosen Kaisha; Fukushima Spinning & Weaving Co. (former Osaka Hosiery Spinning & Weaving Co.), 1912. Address: Hibarigaoka, Kawanishi-machi, Hyogo-ken. — p. 986 ([scan part 1, leaf 1051](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1051/mode/1up))

**HORI, Keijiro 堀啓次郎** Mem. House of Peers; Adviser Osaka Shosen Kaisha; Dir. Sumitomo Bank; b. Jan. 1867, Ishikawa-ken; s. of Gohei Hori, later adopted by late Kasumi Hori. Career: grad. Law Coll. **HORI, Yoshiatsu 堀義貴** Mng.-Dir. Domei National News Agency; b. Feb. [?], Kagoshima-ken; s. of Yukio Hori; m. Fusa, nee Nakajima. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1908; entered diplomatic service 1908; Priv. Legislation Bureau 1932; Chief Secretary of Saito Cabinet 1932-34. Address: 27 Takata Oimatsu-cho, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo. — p. 987 ([scan part 1, leaf 1052](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1052/mode/1up))

**HORINOUCHI, Kensuke 堀内謙介** Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs Apr. 1936; b. 1886, Hyogo-ken; s. of Reijun Horinouchi. Career: grad. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1910; apptd. Yasuko, d. of Chikashi Daito. Career: grad. Metall. Dept. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1911; became Engr. Hitachi Mines; same Saganoseki Smelter 1916; rec'd deg. 1932. **KURASONO, Sanshiro 藏園三四郎** M.P.; b. Jan. 1869, Kagoshima-ken; adopted s. of Jiro Kurasono. Career: grad. Nihon Univ.; elected M.P. 5 times since 1924, Parl. Vice-Min. of Ry. 1935-36. **OKUMURA, Masao 奥村政雄** Pres. Daido Match Co.; Nippon Match Joint Sales Co.; Nippon Carb. Ind. Co.; Dir. Kyushu Elec-Transmission Co., Toyo Nitrogen Ind. Co., Manchou Chem. Ind. **OZAKI, Yukio 尾崎行雄** M.P.; b. Nov. 1859, Miye-ken; s. of Yukimasa Ozaki, samurai. Career: grad. Keio Univ.; Editor Yubin Hochi Shimbun, Niigata Shimbun; Commr. Address: 1774 Hiro, Zushi-machi, Kanagawa-ken. — p. 1041 ([scan part 1, leaf 1106](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1106/mode/1up))

**OZAWA, Keizaburo 小澤啓三郎** Wholesale Dealer in Woollen Goods and Upholstery; b. Mar. 1896, Tottori-ken; s. of Yotaro Ozawa, farmer. Career: engaged in present business since 1912. Address: 18 Awaji-machi 3-chome, Higashi-ku, Osaka. — p. 1041 ([scan part 1, leaf 1106](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1106/mode/1up))

**OZAWA, Nobuyoshi 小澤信義** Vice-Dir. North Chosen Ry. Supt. Bureau, S. M. R.; b. Apr. 1888, Ishikawa-ken; s. of late Tokuhei Ozawa. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. Sch. 1911; joined present firm; Chief, Land Transportation Dept. Harbour Office 1919; went to Europe & America for study 1924; Chief, Gen. Affairs Dept. Anshan Iron Works 1926; Chief, Work Sec. Planning Dept. 1930; Chief, Harbour Sec. 1931. Address: 11 Hokeido, Seishin, Chosen. — p. 1041 ([scan part 1, leaf 1106](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1106/mode/1up))

**OZONE, Sadamatsu 小曾根貞松** Pres. Hanshin Iron Works, Kobe Gas Co., Amagasaki Gas Co., Kobe Elec. Mfg. Works, Velvet Soap Mfg. Co., Tokiwa Co. Ltd.; Dir. Sanyo Hide & Leather Mfg. Co., Japan-Brazil Colonization Co., Nippon Woollen Cloth Co., Oriental Hotel Ltd.; Maya Cable-way Co.; b. Apr. 1879, Kobe; s. of Kiichiro Ozone; m. Kiyo, sister of Tanehiko Yoshida. Career: became Kobe Muni. Councillor; Standing Mem. Kobe Chamber of Com. & Ind. Address: 5 Sakuragi-cho 3-chome, Suma-ku, Kobe. — p. 1041 ([scan part 1, leaf 1106](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1106/mode/1up))

### P

**Pai Min-tzang 白銘璋** Mng.-Dir. & Chief Engr. Manshu Colliery Co. since 1934; b. Apr. 1893, Fengtien Prov. Career: grad. Mining & Metallurgical Dept. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1923; served at Fushun Coal Mines. Three Eastern Prov. Arsenal: Chief Engr. Sian Coal Mines; Councillor Hokang Coal Mines; Pres. Sian Colliery Co.; Adviser Mukden Agr. & Mining Office; Secr. of Manchoukuo Privy Council. Address: Hsinghua-kai Si Ssu-ma-lu, Hsinking. — p. 1041 ([scan part 1, leaf 1106](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1106/mode/1up))

**PANSING, Paul** Hon. Vice-Consul for Finland at Dairen; Merchant; b. Dec. 1888, Germany. Address: 212 Yamagata-dori, Dairen. — p. 1041 ([scan part 1, leaf 1106](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1106/mode/1up))

**PAO Hsi 寶熙** Councillor Manchoukuo Imp. Household Dept. since 1937; b. 1871, Manchuria. Career: Chief Home Affairs Dept. Chief Executive Office 1932-34; Privy Councillor 1934-37. Address: Imp. Household Dept. Hsinking. — p. 1041 ([scan part 1, leaf 1106](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1106/mode/1up))

**PAO Kang 葆康** Gov. Fengtien Prov. since 1934; b. Sept. 1892, Fengtien Prov.; s. of Pao Fu-jun. Career: grad. Mukden Mil. Acad. 1914; served Mukden Mil. Gov.'s Office; Chief Mil. Affairs Sec.; Mukden Mil. Provisions Dept. 1922; Spec. Committee Chinese Eastern Ry.; High Adviser Tung Sheng Spec. Dist. 1929; Vice-Min. of Civil Affairs 1932-34. Address: Gov.'s residence, Mukden. — p. 1041 ([scan part 1, leaf 1106](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1106/mode/1up))

**PARAVICINI, Fritz** M.D.; Medical Practioner; b. 1874, Ennenda, Glarus, Switzerland; n. Swiss; s. of Emil Paravicini, physician. Career: studied at Swiss Schools and Univ.; after receiving degrees in Switzerland, served as Asst. and Locumtenens at Univ.-Clinics and Hospitals of Basle, Berne, Zurich, Engadine, and German Hospital, London; P.-G. work in Germany, France, U.S.A.; in charge of Sanatorium near Zurich; practised in Switzerland and Milan; in Yokohama and Tokyo since 1905; Med. Officer to Brit. Emb. Tokyo 1921-28; visited prisoners' camps on behalf of Int'l Red Cross Committee during World War; delegate of same Committee at Red Cross Conf. 1926, 1934 and 1937 in Tokyo; Swiss Del. at World Educ. Conf. Tokyo 1937. Address: 772 Honmoku 3-chome, Yokohama. — p. 1041 ([scan part 1, leaf 1106](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1106/mode/1up))

**PASQUET, Maurice** American Vice-Consul at Dairen since 1937; b. July 1902, Newport, Rhode Island, U. S. A.; s. of Pierre Paul Pasquet; m. Suzanne Rambaut. Career: American Consulate General, Paris, 1925-31; vice-Consul, Paris, 1931-34; Glasgow, Scotland, 1934-37. Address: 35 Yanagi-machi, Dairen. — p. 1041 ([scan part 1, leaf 1106](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1106/mode/1up))

**PO Ti-hua 博棣華** Teacher Fukushima Higher Com. Sch.; b. July 1892, Peking, China; s. of Po Jui-hsun. Address: 12 Seiyozan, Fukushima-shigai. — p. 1042 ([scan part 1, leaf 1107](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1107/mode/1up))

**PEARCE, Reginald Worth** Danish Consul at Kobe & Osaka; b. 1876, Stourbridge, Worcestershire, England; s. of Horace Pearce, merchant. Career: grad. Hereford Coll. Herefordshire England; Fruit Farming in California 1894-98; served in Sale & Co. Yokohama 1899-1908; engaged in trade as Pres. "Pearce & Co." Yokohama 1908; removed to Kobe 1923; Danish Consul 1929. Address, (home) 66 Kitanocho 4-chome, Kobe. (Office) 92 Yedo-machi, Kobe. — p. 1042 ([scan part 1, leaf 1107](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1107/mode/1up))

**PERKINS, P. D** M.A. (Univ. of San Francisco, Calif.); Bibliographer & Prof. of English; b. Jan. 1897, Windsor, Vermont, U.S.A.; s. of Karl W. Perkins; m. Ione Bendel. Career: for 15 years, business executive; Prof. of English Daisan Koto Gakko since 1935; Co-founder and first research fellow of "Soc. for Oriental Studies" of San Francisco, Calif. Address: Sanko Kansha, Kyoto. — p. 1042 ([scan part 1, leaf 1107](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1107/mode/1up))

**PHIPPS, Gerald Hastings** H. B. M. Cons.-Gen. Seoul Korea since Feb. 1935; b. June 1882; s. of Eccleston A. E. Phipps; m. Aline M. Purvis. Career: apptd. Student Interpreter in Japan Oct. 1903; H. B. M. Vice-Cons. Tokyo 1915; Cons. Tamsui 1920; Honolulu 1925; Kobe 1932. Address: Brit. Consulate-General Keijo Chosen. — p. 1042 ([scan part 1, leaf 1107](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1107/mode/1up))

**PIGGOTT, Francis Steward Gilderoy** Major-General; C.B., D.S.O.; British Military Attache in Tokyo 1921-26 and since 1936; b. Mar. 1880 in London; s. of Sir Francis T. Piggott, barrister-at-law; one time legal adviser to Prime Minister Ito of Japan 1888-91; later attorney-gen. of Mauritius; chief justice of Hongkong; m. Jane Smith. Career: educ. at Cheltenham Coll., Royal Military Acad., Woolwich; Captain 1911; Major 1916; Colonel 1923; Major-Gen. 1935; served in Great War; General Staff, War Office London 1914, 1920-21, 1927-30; Deputy Mil. Secr. to Sec. of State for War 1930-35. Address: British Embassy, Tokyo. — p. 1042 ([scan part 1, leaf 1107](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1107/mode/1up))

**PINTO, J. A. Abranches** Prof. Tokyo Sch. of Foreign Languages; Hon. Consul for Portugal at Tokyo; b. Nov. 1893, Cabanas, Conselho do Carregal do Sal. Portugal; s. of F. do Nascimento Pinto, army officer; m. Tsurue (Japanese). Career: Instituto Superior de Agronomia de Lisboa. Address: 32 Honcho-dori 5-chome, Nakano-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1042 ([scan part 1, leaf 1107](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1107/mode/1up))

**PREIBISCH, Werner** Dr. phil et dipl. ès Lettres; Prof. Lecturer of Yamaguchi Higher Sch. & Yamaguchi Higher Com. Sch.; b. Nov. 1896, Ohlau, Germany; s. of Prof. Dr. Karl Preibisch. Career: graduate of Magdeburg Coll.; Captain of German Army 1914-19; studied Philosophy and Roman Philology at Halle and Muenster, Siena (Italy), Sevilla (Spain), Paris et Besancon (France); Governor of Princes of Hessia; Prof. of High Schools; German Coll. at Athens (Greece). Address: Koto Gakko Kansha, Itoyone, Yamaguchi City. — p. 1042 ([scan part 1, leaf 1107](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1107/mode/1up))

**PRICE, Willard** B.A.; M.A.; Writer; b. 1887 in Canada; s. of Albert M. Price; m. Mary Virginia Selden. Career: grad. Western Res. Univ.; post grad. Columbia Univ., New York Univ.; editorial staff The Survey; editor World Outlook, etc.; studied Indian labour question in S. America; War reconstruction service in France, Italy; dir. motion picture expedition, Sahara desert; ethnographic studies of Battaks of Sumatra etc.; author "Ancient Peoples at New Tasks," "The Negro Round the World," "Study of American Influence in the Orient," "Japan's New Horizons" etc. Address: 2132 Isshiki, Hayama, Japan. — p. 1042 ([scan part 1, leaf 1107](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1107/mode/1up))

### R

**RATJEN, Rudolf** Pres. Rud. Ratjen & Co. Tokyo, Osaka, Dairen; b. Mar. 1881 at Hoya, Germany. Arrived in Japan 1903; founded own firm 1913. Address: 6-34, Aoyama Kita-machi, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1042 ([scan part 1, leaf 1107](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1107/mode/1up))

**RAYVID, Nicolas** Counsellor U.S.S.R. Emb. Tokyo; b. 1897, Moscow; s. of Jacob Rayvid. Career: Attaché to Emb. Berlin 1925; 2nd Secr. same 1926-28; Asst.-Dir. 2nd Western Dept. Foreign Office Moscow 1928-30; Counsellor, Legation, Sweden 1930-31; Dir. 1st Western Dept. Foreign Office, Moscow. Address: U.S.S.R. Embassy, Tokyo. — p. 1042 ([scan part 1, leaf 1107](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1107/mode/1up))

**DEL RE, Arundell** M.A., Balliol College (Oxon), M.A. (London); Chev. of the Corona d'Italia; O.B.E.; Prof. of English Language and Literature, Taihoku Imp. Univ.; Royal Italian Consular Agent, Taihoku; b. Jan. 1892, Florence, Italy; s. of Pietro del Re, Capt. Italian Army, retired; m. H. Joan George. Career: Priv. Sec. to Italian Mil. Attaché, London 1916-19; Lecturer in Italian, Univ. of Oxford and King's Coll. London 1920-27; Prof. of Eng. Lit. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1927-30. Address: c/o Taihoku Imp. Aug. 1899, Sheldon, Missouri, U.S.A.; s of J. J. Reed, Christian minister; m. Josephine L. Reed. Career: arrived Japan 1921; Teacher Himeji and Tatsuno Middle Schs. 1921-23; Pastor First M. E. Church Yalesville Conn. 1925-26; Teacher & Dean Palmore Inst. Kobe 1926-31; author of "Facing Our Social World, 1929". Address: Kwansai Gakuin, Nishinomiya-shigai, Hyogo-ken. — p. 1042 ([scan part 1, leaf 1107](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1107/mode/1up))

Nederland Royal Mail Line (Java Line) 1921; Second visit to Japan 1922; Secr. Head Office, same at Batavia 1923-25; Mem. of Hofmann, Schoffer & Co. in Holland 1930; Mem. Amsterdam Chamber of Com. 1931; connected with Holland-Steamship Co. since 1937. Address: Keizersgracht 517, Amsterdam. — p. 1042 ([scan part 1, leaf 1107](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1107/mode/1up))

**REIFSNIDER, Charles Shriver** B.A.; M.A.; L.H.D.; D.D.; Pres. Rikkyo Daigaku since 1912; Bishop and Educator; b. Nov. 1875, Frederick, Maryland, U. S. A.; n. American; s. of Charles David Reifsnider, railroad man. Career: grad. Kenyon Coll. and Bexley Theological Seminary; ordained Deacon 1900; Priest 1901; Rector, Christ Church, Hudson, Ohio 1900-01; Missionary to Japan since 1901; at Nara 1902-03; Fukui 1903-12; consecrated Bishop 1924. Address: Rikkyo Daigaku, Ikebukuro, Tokyo. — p. 1042 ([scan part 1, leaf 1107](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1107/mode/1up))

**REISCHAUER, August Karl** B.A.; M.A.; D.D.; LL.D.; Missionary & Educator; b. Sept. 1879, Jonesboro, Ill., U. S. A.; s. of Robert Reischauer; m. Helen Sidwell Oldfather. Career: grad. Hanover Coll.; Presb. Theol. Sem. Chicago; Grad. work at Univ. of Chicago and Union Theol. Sem. New York; Prof. Meiji Gakuin 1905-30; Nihon Shin Gakko 1930; Co-founder & Executive Secr. of Tokyo Joshi Daigaku 1917; lectured on Buddhism at various univs. in U. S. A.; Delegate Int'l Missionary Conf. Jerusalem 1928; author of "Studies in Japanese Buddhism," etc. Address: Tokyo Joshi Daigaku, Suginami-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1043 ([scan part 1, leaf 1108](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1108/mode/1up))

**RENNIE, William** B.A.; Ordained missionary; b. Nov. 1866, Toronto, Canada; s. of William Rennie. Career: grad. Address: 37 Hitomi-cho, Hakodate, Hokkaido. — p. 1043 ([scan part 1, leaf 1108](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1108/mode/1up))

**REYNAUD, Louis** French Consul at Harbin; b. Apr. 1884, Paris. Career: French Consular Service in the Far East for 29 years. Address: French Consulate, 11 Tsitsiharskaya St. Harbin. — p. 1043 ([scan part 1, leaf 1108](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1108/mode/1up))

**RI Han-eki 李範益** Governor Chientao Prov.; b. in Chosen. Career: served Chosen Govt. for 30 years; Gov. Chuseinando Prov.; Mem. The Central Council of Chosen; present post since Sept. 1937. Address: Chientao Prov. Office, Chientao, Manchoukuo. — p. 1043 ([scan part 1, leaf 1108](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1108/mode/1up))

**RIN, Yuko 林熊光** Pres. Taisei Fire & Marine Ins. Co. since 1925; b. Mar. 1897; bro. of Yucho Rin. Career: grad. Peers' Sch. and Econ. Course, Tokyo Imp. **ROBINSON, Oswald Richard** M.A.; Barrister-at-law; b. Jan. 1868, London; s. of Sir John R. Robinson, editor & mgr. of The Daily News; m. Alice Maud Curtis of Harwich, England. Career: Westminster School, Trin. Coll., Camb.; called to the bar 1896; practised 20 years patent law; came to Japan 1922 to Saga High Sch.; lectured 8 years Law & Lit. at Kyushu Imp. Univ. Address: Nishi Shirage Koji, Saga City. — p. 1043 ([scan part 1, leaf 1108](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1108/mode/1up))

**RODRIGUEZ Y Jimenez de Acevedo, Carlos de** Ph, G.; C.a.L.; R.P.D.; Venezuelan Cons.-General in Japan since 1931; b. Aug. 1899, Upata Dto-Piar Bolivar-State, Venezuela, S. Court; 1st Civil Ct.; Sup. Ct. 1927; Dir. Polit. & Adm. Dept. of Bol. Sta. 1928-30; Gen. Secr. a.i. of same Govt. 1930-31; Ven. Del. 15th Intl. Red Cross Conf. Tokyo 1935; 7th Educ. Intl. Conf. Tokyo 1937; author of "Venezuela" 1933 Tokyo and "Asia America." Club: American Club Tokyo. Address: 664 Marunouchi Bldg. Tokyo; P. O. Box 604 Central Tokyo; 20 Yamate-cho, Yokohama. — p. 1043 ([scan part 1, leaf 1108](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1108/mode/1up))

**ROLDAN Leopoldo Borda** Charge d'Affaires of Colombia since 1937; b. Aug. 1898 at Bogota, Colombia; s. of Alberto Borda Tanco, former rector of the Tech. Univ. of Bogota; Hon. Prof. of Univ. of Colombia; Mem. Colombian Acad. of Sciences; m. Suzanne Weiprecht. Career: studied Civil Engrg. Nat. Univ. of Bogota; Secr. Comm. Attache, Paris, 1918-30; Dir. Gen. of Public Educ. for Bogota and Cundinamarca, 1930-33; Mem. Colombian Acad. of Educ.; 1st Secr. Colombian Leg. in Ecuador, 1933; Charge d'Affaires ad-interim to Ecuador, 1934-36; Comm. Orden del Merito of Ecuador. Address: Yusen Bldg., Marunouchi, Tokyo. — p. 1043 ([scan part 1, leaf 1108](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1108/mode/1up))

**ROMER, Tadeusz** Polish Minister to Japan since 1937; b. Dec. 1894; s. of Bronislaw Romer, prop. of land estate; married. Career: grad. Univ. Lausanne, Switzerland; 1st Secr. Embassy Paris 1919-21; assigned to Foreign Office Warsaw 1921: acting chief, Western Sec. 1923-25; chief of same, 1925-27; counsellor Embassy, Rome 1928-34; minister to Portugal, 1935-37. Address: 9 Mita Tsuna-machi, Tokyo. — p. 1043 ([scan part 1, leaf 1108](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1108/mode/1up))

**de ROOS, Willem Hendrikus** Acting Netherlands Consul-General in Kobe since 1934: Knight of the Order of Orange Nassau; b. Feb. 1895 at Wageningen, Netherlands. Career: educ. course of Oriental studies, Univ. of Leyden; apptd. student-interpreter 1921; arrived in Japan 1921; 1st class interpreter 1926. Address: Meikai Bldg. 32 Akashi-machi, Kobe. — p. 1043 ([scan part 1, leaf 1108](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1108/mode/1up))

**ROSENBERG, Karl** Dipl. Ing.; Engr.; b. Feb. 1894, Aachen, Germany. Address: 907 Magome-machi 2-chome, Omori-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1043 ([scan part 1, leaf 1108](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1108/mode/1up))

**RUTHE, Alfred E** Hon. Consul for Estonia at Dairen; b. 1888, Estonia. Address: 54 Yamagata-dori, Dairen. — p. 1043 ([scan part 1, leaf 1108](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1108/mode/1up))

Univ. 1914; entered Finance Office; Chief, Shimokyo Taxation Office; Commr. Tsingtao Garrison Civil Adm. Office 1915; Mem. of Suite, Japanese Delagation to 1st & 6th League of Nations Assemblies; 1st Secr. Legation, Stockholm; Chief, 1st & 2nd Secs. Cultural Work Dept. Foreign Office. Dept.; Councillor Ry. Bureau; Ry. Inspector; Chief Gen. Affairs Sec. Traffic Bureau; Secr. to Ry. Minister; Dir. Board of Tourist Ind. 1932-34; Dir. Harbin Ry. Adm. Bureau 1934-36. Kobe; Organizer & Pres. Indian Nat. Cong. Committee of Japan, Indo-Japanese Young Peoples' Assn.; b. Sept. 1898, Bhagalpore, India; s. of Lal Mohan Sahay, landlord. **SAIJO, Yaso 西條八十** Poet; Prof. French Litt. Waseda Univ.; b. Jan. 1892, Tokyo; s. of Jubei Saijo, soap mfg. Career: grad. Litt. Course, Waseda Univ.; studied at Japanese Litt. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; sent to Europe by Waseda Univ. to study at Paris and Sorbonne Univs. 1924-26; then travelled to England and Italy; author of "Gold Dust," "Unacquainted Lover," "Beautiful Forfeiture," "Collection of Folk Songs," etc. Address: 377 Kashiwagi 3-chome, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1044 ([scan part 1, leaf 1109](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1109/mode/1up))

Institute for Nutrition, Tokyo. m. Shigeko, d. of Takinosuke Amano. Career: grad. Med. Coll. Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1924; Dr. Kyoto Imp. Univ. Hospital; studied medicine under Prof. Thanhause and Prof. Stepp at Freiburg and Munich. **SAIONJI, Kinmochi 西園寺公望** Prince; Genro; Mem. House of Peers; b. Oct. 1849, Kyoto; s. of late Kimizumi Tokudaiji and later adopted by Morosue Saionji. System 1882; Minister to Austria 1885; to Germany 1887; Grand Chancellor, Imp. Orders 1891-94; Vice-pres. House of Peers 1894; Privy Councillor 1894; Min. of Educ. 1894 and 1898; Foreign Min. 1895 and 1896; Finance Min. and Premier 1901; Pres. Seiyukai 1903; formed cabinet 1903 and 1911; Chief Delegate to World Peace Conf. 1919. Address: 5 Minami Kogacho, Surugadai, Kanda-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1044 ([scan part 1, leaf 1109](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1109/mode/1up))

Emb. London 1918; Mem. of Suite, Delegation to Peace Conf. Paris 1919; 2nd Secr. Emb. London; attended 1st League of Nations Assembly Geneva 1920; Consul Seattle 1921; Consul-Gen. New York 1923; Dir. **TANAKA, Tomoenosuke (Chigaku) 田中巴之助** Hon. Pres. Kokuchukai; Chairman Meijikai and Kokusei Bungei-kai; Prop. Daily Dai-Nippon; b. Nov. 1861, Tokyo; s. of Yoshiatsu Minamoto (popular as Genryu Tada), physician; m. 1897. Career: in 1877, after being tormented with sceptism was awakened to the fact of the spirit of nationalism having not sufficiently spread and then devoted himself to studies; in 1881 started propagation of nationalism and has worked in that cause by pen and speech for the past half century founding two patriotic societies "Kokuchukai" and "Meijikai" in the interval; in 1929 had Imp. Cup conferred upon him in recognition of his meritorious services in the cause of education and also certificate awarded by Education Department for the same; successfully conducted petition movement for 4 years for institution of the "Meijisetsu"; started campaign for upholding the cause of the national polity by taking the opportunity of the success of the said petition movement; on May 11, 1935 opened "New lecture on the National Polity of Japan" and started a monthly for the purpose; in June, 1935 went over to Manchoukuo and lectured on the national polity in the presence of the Emperor; after return home via Chosen set about editing "Shishiwo Zenshu." Address: c/o Shinkoen, Ichinoe-machi, Edogawa-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1063 ([scan part 1, leaf 1128](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1128/mode/1up))
