Coll. 1913; Magistrate, Kianghun-Tao, Ichang-Tao, 1921; Chief, Ki-Hei Salt Transportation Office after Mukden Incident, 1931; Chief, State Salt Transportation Office, 1934-37. Address: Manshu Kogyo Ginko, Hsinking, Manchoukuo. — p. 1075 ([scan part 1, leaf 1140](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1140/mode/1up))

**WENNEKER, Paul W** Captain; German Nav. Attache to Tokyo since 1933; b. Feb. 27, 1890; s. of Franz Wenneker. Career: entered naval service 1909; during World War was on board cruiser "Mainz" which sunk at the battle of Heligoland; after the War became gunnery officer and attached to the Staff of the Commander-in-Chief of the fleet. Address: 202 Yoyogi Sanya, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1075 ([scan part 1, leaf 1140](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1140/mode/1up))

**WHITE, Oswald** C.M.G.; Brit. Cons.-Gen. at Osaka; b. Sept. 1884, Newcastle-on-Tyne; n. British; s. of James White, merchant. Career: entered consular service 1903; Vice-Cons. 1913; Cons. 1920; Cons.-Gen. 1927. Address: Brit. Consulate-General, Osaka. — p. 1075 ([scan part 1, leaf 1140](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1140/mode/1up))

**WIERSUM, Menno Simon** Mng.-Dir. M. S. Wiersum & Co., Yokohama; Consul for Netherlands, Yokohama; b. 1878, Kantens, Netherlands; n. Dutch; s. of L. Wiersum. Career: grad. Hoogere Burger Sch. Groningen; business practice at Groningen and Hamburg 6 years; at Shanghai, Hankow and Yokohama 1901-05; joined Simon, Evers & Co., Yokohama 1905; started business on his account 1915. Address: 25 Yamashita-cho, Yokohama. — p. 1075 ([scan part 1, leaf 1140](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1140/mode/1up))

**WISTRAND, Hugo** D.L.; 1st Secr. Swedish Legation, Tokyo; b. April 1895 at Stockholm. Address: 451 Shirokane Sanko-cho, Tokyo. — p. 1075 ([scan part 1, leaf 1140](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1140/mode/1up))

**WOHLERS, H** Merchant; b. Oct. 1898, Hamburg, Germany; m. Liesel Krueger; n. German. Address: c/o Bergmann & Co., Hachiman-dori 3-chome, Kobe. — p. 1075 ([scan part 1, leaf 1140](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1140/mode/1up))

**WOODD, Frederick Hampden Basil** M.A. (Cambridge Univ.); Missionary, Priest of Nippon Seikokai; b. Mar. 1906, Osaka; s. of Rev. Charles Hampden Basil Woodd; m. Foss, Emily Hornby, 1936. Career: born in Japan; returned to England 1913; educated at Weymouth Coll. and Cambridge Univ. (Jesus Coll.); ordained Deacon England; came back to Japan 1933; with Momoyama Chugakko; Priest-in-charge of Fukkatsu Kyokwai, 1929; Priest 1930; 3 years Curacy in Tonbridge in Osaka. Address: 61 Asahi-cho 2-chome, Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka. — p. 1075 ([scan part 1, leaf 1140](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1140/mode/1up))

**WUCHERPFENNIG, Hermann** Dr. phil.; Kammersänger; Bass Singer; Prof. Imp. Academy of Music, Ueno since 1932; b. June 1884, Mühlhausen in Thüringen; n. German; s. of Franz Wucherpfennig, official. Career: grad. Univ. of Berlin 1922; studied singing under Prof. R. von Milde and Morattl of Milano, Italy 1912; sang 25 years in opera stages and concerts at Dessau, Nürnberg, Düsseldorf, Berlin, Karlsruhe, Frankfurt, Dresden, Cöln, Wiesbaden, Stuttgart; went to Norway, Hungary, South America and Italy for performance; kept private singing sch. in Karlsruhe 1922-30. Address: 1855 Sanno 2-chome, Omori-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1075 ([scan part 1, leaf 1140](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1140/mode/1up))

**YABUKI, Keiki 矢吹慶輝** D. Litt.; Prof. Taisho Univ.; b. Feb. 1879, Fukushima-ken; s. of Tomeshichi, farmer. Career: grad. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Chief, Tokyo Social Bureau 1925-26; Asst. Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1924-35; sent to Europe and America 1913-16 and 1922-33. Address: 365 Takinogawa, Takinogawa-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1075 ([scan part 1, leaf 1140](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1140/mode/1up))

**YABUKI, Seizo 矢吹省三** Baron; Mem. House of Peers; Pres. Fuji Life Ins. Co.; b. July 1883, Tokyo; s. of late Hideichi Yabuki, Lieut.-Gen. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908; joined Yokohama Specie Bank; became Dir. of several firms; elected Peer 1918; Parl. Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs 1925-27; of Navy 1929-31; of Foreign Affairs 1931; of Finance 1934-36. Address: 45 Nampeidai, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1075 ([scan part 1, leaf 1140](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1140/mode/1up))

**YADA, Shichitaro 矢田七太郎** Manchoukuo Privy Councillor since 1934; b. Dec. 1879, Shizuoka-ken; bro. of Shusaku Yada. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1906; Elève-Consul at Canton, Hankow and Tientsin; Diplomatic Probationer in China; Secr., Embassy in Italy; Consul-Gen. at San Francisco, London and Shanghai; Minister to Switzerland 1929-33; attended Gen. Disarm. Conf. Geneva 1931. Address: c/o Sangifu, Hsinking. — p. 1075 ([scan part 1, leaf 1140](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1140/mode/1up))

**YAGI, Motohachi 八木元八** Dir. Yalu Timber Co.; b. Feb. 1873, Shizuoka-ken; s. of Magohachi Yagi, merchant. Career: studied in China & Russia; Vice-Consul at several places; Consul, Tsingtao, China & New Orleans; Consul-Gen. Harbin. Address: c/o Yalu Timber Co., Antung, Manchoukuo. — p. 1075 ([scan part 1, leaf 1140](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1140/mode/1up))

**YAGI, Toshiharu 八木壽治** Pres. Educ. Inst. of S. M. R. since 1934; b. Feb. 1885, Tottori-ken; s. of Eijiro Morimoto. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Normal Sch. 1908; Teacher Miye Pref. Girls' Normal Sch.; Prin. Anshan Primary Sch.; Dir. Fushun & Mukden Higher Girls' Schs. Address: 11 Aoi-cho, Mukden. — p. 1075 ([scan part 1, leaf 1140](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1140/mode/1up))

**YAMADA, Kosçak 山田耕筰** Pres. Japan Symphony Assn.; Composer; Adviser Takarazuka Opera, Columbia Gramaphone Co., etc.; b. June 1886, Tokyo; s. of Kenzo Yamada. Career: grad. Mid. Sch. Course, Kwansei Gakuin and Tokyo Academy of Music, Ueno; studied in Germany and grad. Composition Dept., Kaiser's Conservatoire, Berlin; conducted orchestras in America; founded Philharmony Society; composed songs, orchestras, symphonies and operas; founded Music-Drama Assn. and Composers' Assn. Address: 19 Goban-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1075 ([scan part 1, leaf 1140](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1140/mode/1up))

**YAMADA, Ninzo 山田忍三** Mng.-Dir. Shirokiya Dept. Store since 1927; b. Dec. 1885, Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Masanari Namiyama, later adpt. by Ryuichi Yamada. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1905; established Yamada Shokai 1924; agent for Japan of Ford Motor Co.; founded Yamada Pub. Co. Address: 65 Gotanda 5-chome, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1075 ([scan part 1, leaf 1140](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1140/mode/1up))

**YAMADA, Otozo 山田乙三** Lieut.-Gen.; Comdr. 12th Div.; b. 1881, Nagano-ken; s. of Kaku Ichikawa; later adopted by Takayuki Yamada. Career: grad. Mil. Acad. 1903; Instructor Mil. Cav. Sch.; Comdr. Cav. 26th Reg.; Chief Gen. Affairs Dept. Chosen Army Staff Office; Instructor Mil. Staff Coll.; Chief, Educational Dept. Mil. Cav. Sch. 1930; Chief Gen. Affairs Sec. Gen. Staff Office; Dir. Mil. **YAMADA, Saburo 山田三良** D.L.; Dir. Soc. for Int'l Cultural Relations; Emeritus Prof. Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Nov. 1869, Nara-ken; s. of Heizaburo Yamada. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1896; studied in Europe & Amer. 1897; Prof. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1901-30; Pres. Keijo Imp. Univ. 1931-35. Address: 172 Benten-cho, Ushigome-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1076 ([scan part 1, leaf 1141](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1141/mode/1up))

**YAMADA, Sanjiro 山田三次郎** Chairman Shoko Glass Co., Asahi Glass Co.; b. Aug. 1870, Kagoshima-ken; s. of Ariyasu Yamada. Career: Dir. Takachiho Brick Refinery. Address: 103 Aoyama Minami-cho 2-chome, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1076 ([scan part 1, leaf 1141](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1141/mode/1up))

**YAMADA, Tatsuo 山田龍雄** Mint-Master Finance Office; b. Nov. 1893, Kochi-ken; s. of Chojitsu Yamada. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1918; entered Finance Dept.; Chief Mito & Kyobashi Revenue Offices; Commr. Revenue Supt. Bureau; Chief Accounts Sec. Tokyo Revenue Supt. **YAMADA, Umajiro 山田馬次郎** Pres. Okura Bldg. Co.; Dir. Manshu Pulp Mfg. Co., Showa Steel Works, Ishikawajima Aircraft Co., Japan Wireless Telephone & Telegraph Co., Okura-gumi; b. Address: 4 Onden 4-chome, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1076 ([scan part 1, leaf 1141](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1141/mode/1up))

**YAMAGATA, Kiyoshi 山形清** Chief Documents Sec. Foreign Office; b. 1893, Ibaraki-ken. Career: grad. Law Coll. Tokyo Imp. **YAMAGISHI, Keinosuke 山岸慶之助** Aud. Kirin Brewery Co.; b. May 1878, Tokyo; s. of Yubei Kitagawa, and later adopted by Kura Yamagishi. Career: grad. Tokyo Higher Com. **YAMAGUCHI, Kisaburo 山口喜三郎** Ph. D.; Pres. Tokyo Elec. Co.; Dir. Daido Signal Co., Asahi Electrification Ind. Co., Tokyo Elec. Radio Co., Shibaura Engrg. Works; b. **YAMAGUCHI, Sotoji 山口外二** Chief Operation Office, Operating & Mech. Engrg. Dept. Gen. Direction of Manchoukuo State Ry. since 1936; b. Mar. 1889, Fukui-ken; s. of Rizaemon Yamaguchi. **YAMAMOTO, Hidesuke 山本英輔** Admiral on the Reserve list. (See 1936 issue). — p. 1076 ([scan part 1, leaf 1141](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1141/mode/1up))

**YAMAMOTO, Isoroku 山本五十六** Vice-Admiral; Vice-Min. of Navy; b. Apr. 1884, Niigata-ken; s. of Teikichi Takano; later adopted by Tamashi Yamamoto. Career: grad. Nav. **Stock-Breeding Association, Central** —Est. 1915. Issues a magazine. Mem. 6,000. Pres. Baron S. Hirayama. Address: 2, Marunouchi 3-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1214 ([scan part 1, leaf 1279](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1279/mode/1up))

**Suikosha (Naval Club)** —Est. 1876. Naval officers' social club with membership of over 12,129, publishes a bulletin. Pres. Adm. O. Nagano (Naval Minister). Address: Sakae-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1214 ([scan part 1, leaf 1279](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1279/mode/1up))

**Suiyo Kwai (The Kyoto Association for Mining & Metallurgy)** —Est. 1900. Publishes The Journal of Mining and Metallurgy, Japanese, three times a year. Mem. 361. Pres. D. Saito, D. Eng. Address: Inst. of Min. & Metal., Kyoto Imp. Univ., Kyoto. — p. 1214 ([scan part 1, leaf 1279](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1279/mode/1up))

**Sunday School Association, National** —Est. 1907. Mem. 915. Sunday Schools. Rep. T. Yamamoto. Address: 6, Nishiki-cho 1-chome, Kanda-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1214 ([scan part 1, leaf 1279](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1279/mode/1up))

### (T)

**Teikoku Fishery Association** —Est. 1924. Publishes a monthly magazine "Teisui." Mem. 43 Fishing Corporations. Pres. Viscount M. Nomura . Address: Sankaido Bldg., Tameike, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1215 ([scan part 1, leaf 1280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1280/mode/1up))

**Teikoku Forestry Association** —Est. 1919. Issues a monthly bulletin. Mem. 127. Pres. H. Honda, D. Agr. Address: Sankaido Bldg., Tameike, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1215 ([scan part 1, leaf 1280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1280/mode/1up))

**Teikoku Hatsumei Kyokai (Society for Protecting Industrial Property)** —Est. 1905. Mem. 3,728. Pres. Baron Y. Sakatani. Address: 10, Marunouchi 3-chome, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1215 ([scan part 1, leaf 1280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1280/mode/1up))

**Teikoku Hiko Kyokai** —(See Imperial Aero Society). — p. 1215 ([scan part 1, leaf 1280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1280/mode/1up))

**Teikoku Kaiji Kyokai (Imp. Marine Assn.)** —Est. 1926. Object, to promote development of industries; publishes a monthly magazine as its organ. Mem. 800. Pres. Baron Y. Sakatani. **Teikoku Kyoiku-kai (Japanese Education Association)** —Est. 1883. An unofficial advisory body in educational matters; published books and magazinees; awards honor to those of meritorious services to education. Mem. 2,245. Pres. H. Nagata. Address: Hitotsubashi-dori, Kanda-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1215 ([scan part 1, leaf 1280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1280/mode/1up))

**Textile Weaving Association, Japan** —Est. 1885. Object, to help development of weaving industry; issues a bulletin. Mem. 1,500. Pres. S. Shibata. Address: Nichibei Shintaku Bldg., Kitamaki-cho, Kyobashi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1215 ([scan part 1, leaf 1280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1280/mode/1up))

**Toa Dobun-kai** —Est. 1899. Maintains schools at Shanghai, Tientsin and Hankow; devoted to the cultural development in Japan and China and the education of Chinese and Japanese desiring to work in China. Mem. 3,000. Pres. Count N. Makino. Address: Sannen-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1215 ([scan part 1, leaf 1280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1280/mode/1up))

**Tohoku Medical Society** —Est. 1916. Issues The Journal, in Japanese, 5 per year. Mem. 1,020. Pres. G. Fuse, M.D. Address: Fac. Med., Tohoku Imp. Univ., Sendai. — p. 1215 ([scan part 1, leaf 1280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1280/mode/1up))

**Tokyo Charity Association** —Est. 1871. Maintains a hospital and a medical college in Tokyo; issues a bulletin. Mem. 932. Pres. Prince I. Tokugawa. Address: Atago-cho, Shiba-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1215 ([scan part 1, leaf 1280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1280/mode/1up))

**Tokyo Club** —Est. 1885. By Japanese and foreigners. Mem. about 420. Pres. H. I. H. Prince Kan-in; Vice-Pres. Baron G. Hayashi; Dir. A. Kabayama; Hon. Secr. J. W. Graham; Treas. Viscount H. Akimoto. Address: Sannen-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1215 ([scan part 1, leaf 1280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1280/mode/1up))

**Tokyo Institute for Municipal Research, The** —Est. 1922. Issues a monthly Journal. Pres. Y. Sakatani. Address: Hibiya, Tokyo. — p. 1215 ([scan part 1, leaf 1280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1280/mode/1up))

**Tokyo Medical Society** —Est. 1886. Issues The Journal, in Japanese, monthly. Mem. 3,000. Chairman H. Nagai. Address: Physiological Inst., Tokyo Imp. Univ., Tokyo. — p. 1215 ([scan part 1, leaf 1280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1280/mode/1up))

**Toyo Kyokai** —(See Oriental Association). — p. 1215 ([scan part 1, leaf 1280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1280/mode/1up))

**Trades Association, Japan** —Est. 1886. Holds meeting monthly and publishes its organ "International Trade," in Japanese, monthly. Mem. 650. Pres. Baron I. Morimura; Vice-Pres. E. Okamoto. Address: 7, Nishi-Ginza 3-chome, Kyobashi-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1215 ([scan part 1, leaf 1280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1280/mode/1up))

### (U)

**University Graduates' Society (Gakushi-kwai)** —Est. 1886. Admits graduates of Imperial Universities of Tokyo, Kyoto, Kyushu, Tohoku and Hokkaido, and others having connection with the above institutions; publishes monthly bulletin; comprises 18 committees and 1 chief secretary. Mem. 41,000. Pres. Baron Y. Sakatani. Address: Nishiki-cho, Kanda-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1215 ([scan part 1, leaf 1280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1280/mode/1up))

### (V)

**Volunteer Nurses Society** —Established as an adjunct of the Japan Red Cross Society (which see), this philanthropic body of women possesses over 18,900 members throughout the country. Chairman Dowager Marchioness Nabeshima. Address: Japan Red Cross Society, Shiba Park, Tokyo. — p. 1215 ([scan part 1, leaf 1280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1280/mode/1up))

### (W)

**Women's Association, Japan** —Est. 1922. Object, to elevate social status of Japanese womanhood. Mem. 200. Pres. Mrs. E. Kaetsu. Address: Atago-cho 1-chome, Shiba-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1215 ([scan part 1, leaf 1280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1280/mode/1up))

**Women's Association, National** —Est. 1899. Aims at promoting women's culturev. Address: Jissen Jogakko, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1215 ([scan part 1, leaf 1280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1280/mode/1up))

**Women's Educational Association, Japan** —Est. 1920. Issues a monthly bulletin. Mem. 10,030. Pres. Marchioness E. Nabeshima. Address: Tenma-cho, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1215 ([scan part 1, leaf 1280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1280/mode/1up))

**Women's Peace Association, Japan** —Est. 1921. Mem. 350. Address: 52, Shinsaka-machi, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1215 ([scan part 1, leaf 1280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1280/mode/1up))

### (Y)

**Yokohama United Club** —Chairman P. Nipkow; Secr. S. R. Kerr. Address: 4, Yamashita-cho, Yokohama. — p. 1215 ([scan part 1, leaf 1280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1280/mode/1up))

**Young Men's League (Japan), Federation of** —Est. 1922. Is the national headquarters and central controlling organ of local young men's leagues all over Japan. Mem. about 260,000. Publishes "Nippon Seinen Shimbun," "Seinen Card" and other pamphlets. Gen.-Dir. Fumio Goto. Address: Young Men's Hall, Kasumigaoka-machi, Yotsuya-ku, Tokyo. — p. 1215 ([scan part 1, leaf 1280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1280/mode/1up))

### (Z)

**Zoological Society of Japan, The** —Est. 1877. Publishes The Zoological Magazine, in Japanese, monthly, and Annotations Zoological Japoneuses in European languages, occasionally. Mem. 607. Pres. N. Yata, D. Sc. Address: Zoo, Inst., Tokyo Imp. Univ., Tokyo. — p. 1215 ([scan part 1, leaf 1280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1280/mode/1up))

**Zymurgy Society of Osaka** —Est. 1910. Publishes The Journal of Zymurgy, in Japanese, twice a month. Mem. 4,500. Pres. Y. Nishiwaki. Address: Osaka Technical College, Osaka. — p. 1215 ([scan part 1, leaf 1280](https://archive.org/details/japan-manchoukuo-year-book-1938/page/n1280/mode/1up))
